Constructions for back diffusion account for this apparent discrepency though are not shown here. 30 6.2 Solid Fraction, Enthalpy Release, and Feeding Estimation of phase fraction behavior during the liquid to solid transition enables important physics to be included in CFD simulations for casting. In particular this impacts both the enthalpy released during solidification (heat flow) and has consequences on the fluid flow characteristics (porosity and macrosegregation). All solidification reactions have an associated enthalpy of fusion which is released at the reaction interface, as already discussed in prior sections, and in non-congruent systems the enthalpy release is over the solidification temperature range. A naive and often default assumption is to express that heat in the simulation linearly as cells experience temperatures from liquidus to the solidus. With greater understanding of the phase relationships and the kinetics, one can make higher fidelity approximations. With more confidence in the choice of phase boundaries, as is provided by this work, one may move a modest, but well justified step further than a simple linear assumption.
